I won’t make any changes until you explicitly confirm. Here’s exactly what I would do and what could go wrong:

Planned action
- Delete rows 210 through 480 (inclusive) on the sheet/tab named "raw" in the spreadsheet you’re referring to.

Risks / what could go wrong
- Wrong sheet or wrong row numbers (off-by-one) and you lose different data.
- If you’re looking at a filtered view, those row numbers might not match the underlying sheet.
- Merged cells, named ranges, or formulas that reference the deleted rows could break or shift.
- Pivot tables that use a hard-coded range (not a dynamic range/table) might not update as you expect.
- If the platform does not provide revision history, deletion may be permanent.

Undoability
- If the spreadsheet supports revision history (e.g., Google Sheets, Excel online), we can usually restore the prior state. If it does not, deletion may be irreversible.

Preservation option (recommended)
- I can first create a backup: duplicate the "raw" tab (e.g., "raw_backup_YYYYMMDD") before deleting. This preserves structure and makes rollback trivial.

Please confirm exactly which of these you want by replying with one of the options below:
1) "Delete rows 210–480 from 'raw' and create backup" — I will duplicate the tab, then delete.
2) "Delete rows 210–480 from 'raw' without backup" — I will delete immediately.
3) "Do not delete" — I will do nothing.

If there are multiple spreadsheets or the sheet name differs, state the spreadsheet name or ID and confirm the sheet is named "raw." Once you confirm one of the options, I will proceed and will first inspect the relevant rows before editing.
